podcast.body: Released in June 1977, around the time Johnny Rotten was subjected to two attacks. This single managed to make it into the top 10 on the charts. "The next one was Pretty Vacant, which came out in June."

podcast.body: This song is mentioned as an example of a successful mashup component when mixed with Madonna's "Ray of Light," illustrating how seemingly disparate tracks can create compelling new juxtapositions. "The order of the juxtaposition, the cooler."

podcast.body: This song is presented as an example from the Sex Pistols, a band whose very existence was intrinsically linked to the "Sex" shop on King's Road, which sold clothing to the emerging British punk subculture. "The sex pistols and pretty vacant, that band would not have existed if it weren't for that store selling clothes to this new British tribe called punks."

podcast.body: This song was originally released as a 7-inch single on Virgin Records in 1977, with the serial number VS184. Some copies included a picture sleeve, and others had a push-out center. According to the Record Collector price guide, a mint condition copy of this 7-inch single is valued at 5 pounds, or just over $11 Canadian, despite an online seller listing a copy for $510 US. "The sex pistols in Pretty Vacant originally released in 1977 as a 7-inch single on Virgin Records, serial number VS184, and worth about $11 dollars."

podcast.body: This song was written by bass player Glenn Matlock, who confessed to drawing inspiration from ABBA's "SOS" when composing it. "The Sex Pistols and Pretty Vacant, written by bass player Glenn Matlock, who confessed to ripping off the Abyssal, SOS, to write it."
